newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan welcomes suspension of Israeli building plan.
newsitem.headline: Annan welcomes suspension of Israeli building plan.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan has welcomed the decision of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to suspend construction of a housing project in East Jerusalem, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Tuesday.
In a telephone call on Monday to Netanyahu, Annan said "he was encouraged by the initiative taken by the prime minister to suspend the latest effort to build housing in East Jerusalem," Eckhard said.
"He told the prime minister that this is the kind of gesture that is needed to get the (Middle East) peace talks back on track, and that of course is the goal of the international community."

Annan told Netanyahu he "felt that was the right decision and applauded the prime minister's courage in making it," Eckhard said. "The prime minister seemed to appreciate the secretary-general's call and his thoughts," the U.N. spokesman added.

At issue was a plan to build 70 Jewish homes in Ras al-Amoud, an Arab neighbourhood on the slopes of the Mount of Olives captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, on land owned by an American Jewish businessman.

Netanyahu blocked the plan after a surprise decision by the Jerusalem municipality to approve construction. His action also has been welcomed by the United States, Britain, France and other countries.

Israel is going ahead with the construction of 6,500 homes at another site on captured territory south of Jerusalem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic. The start of work there in March sparked repeated meetings of the Security Council and the General Assembly.
